profile.headline:
NVIDIA Omniverse Fabric: an OpenUSD-native simulation+rendering data modeling framework.
Game development tools, asset pipelines, and infrastructure.
GDC Advisory Board, GDC Tools Summit, and GDC Tools Roundtables.
profile.summary:
My goal is to be advancing the state-of-the-art of how games and/or realtime software are developed.  I am fascinated by the development process itself, and any technology that can accelerate it.

I pride myself on good communication skills when working with content creators, and I push hard for taking on ambitious goals to try and attain a true zero-latency workflow in game tools.  I see responsive tools design, automatic data processing, and simplicity as necessary features of modern game creation tools.

I have a lot of experience working on content creation tools for making games.  I have implemented numerous infrastructure technologies at different studios, a stand alone 3D level editor from scratch, as well as export pipeline and workflow optimization plugins to top end graphics packages such as Maya, XSI, and 3dsmax.

positions.title: Principal Software Engineer
positions.description: I am working on Omniverse Fabic, which enables USD content to serve realtime simulation applications.

positions.title: Senior Tools Engineer
positions.description:
At Epic I worked on Unreal Engine, in which I contributed:

A new performance analytics pipeline which ran on specialized hardware on the build farm. It used the Trace/UnrealInsights binary logging system to track Cpu and Memory activity. That information was collated into metrics posted to a database. This plotted performance measurements across time to allow of analysis of performance regressions reported by the user base.

Improvements to the Trace/UnrealInsights pipeline including a frontend to capture a snapshot Trace file for incident analysis by engineers, and plumbing new interfaces that allow for external tools to analyze the binary logging data.

positions.title: Director of Tools Technology
positions.description:
I lead the tools team at Infinity Ward.  I work with engineering and content teams to ensure they have the workflow and throughput they need to create the content for the best game experiences in the world.

My team owns the asset pipeline, disc mastering, code and data build distribution, distributed build result caching, continuous integration, automated testing, human+automation communication, and the content creation workflow for the most sophisticated tools in the studio.

Management-wise, I make an effort to experiment and incubate production workflow for balancing backlogs of feature requests against bug triage.  I like to serve as a model for how other teams in the studio could operate, and try to be as transparent as I can.

positions.title: Technical Director
positions.description: I designed and lead implementation of the co-development workflow for operating in symphony with the Tokyo studio.  This included release engineering code and asset merges, juggling multiple perforce repositories, and tooling to give content creators and engineers significantly more flexibility for developing the game.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
I was a software engineer focusing on simulation and visualization software.  I did some OS and architecture porting, build system improvements (building everything from scratch to ease toolchain updates), setting up continuous integration (Jenkins then soon thereafter TeamCity).  I also broke ground on networked object synchronization systems using MongoDB (using its built-in geospatial query support and tailable cursors).

I also did a short stint working on Android Hardware Abstraction (with regards to audio, and which involved making builds of Android itself), and made some custom Linux kernel builds to support a handset device.  This included using ADB, ADK, NDK, and a bit of fiddling with preparing and making flashes.

positions.title: Lead Engineer
positions.description:
I was the leader of the tools team at Neversoft.  Our team tackled making incremental improvements to the Call of Duty engine codebase.  This included the build and packing pipeline, Radiant, and other asset management utilities.

Personally, I deployed a environment management utility within the studio, which greatly aided being able to juggle multiple project titles simultaneously.  I also did some quick-and-dirty asset porting between CoD-engine based titles, and help design new-era content creation tools and pipelines.

I also started the team on a sprint-based management system.  The team did its own task estimation and breakdown, as well as task/bug triage and sprint acceptance.  It was well regarded and (apparently) lived on after my departure.

positions.title: Senior Engineer
positions.description: I architected and implemented many of the core systems and tools within the Helium open source game engine (http://heliumproject.org), an evolution of Insomniac's Nocturnal Initiative open source project.  This involved implementing support for unicode strings, 64-bit builds, and the next major evolution of Reflect, a C++ Reflection library and object automation system.

positions.title: Senior Tools Engineer
positions.description:
I helped architect and implement most all of the game production tools at Insomniac.  This includes our internal frameworks and libraries, plugins to art packages, and level editor.  I also started and administered Insomniac's open source project, Nocturnal Initiative.

I designed and managed the tools release process including branching code in revision control, software versioning, software distribution, error reporting, and user feedback.

positions.title: DCC Plugin Engineer
positions.description:
I maintained and implemented plugins to import/export skeleton and animation data between most major graphics packages: Maya, 3dsmax, Softimage|XSI, Lightwave, and Motionbuilder.

I assisted with mocap character pipeline work within the studio, and helped streamline and test proprietary software within Motion Analysis passive optical motion capture system.

projects.title: Helium Project
projects.description: Helium is an open source game engine.  Its liberally licensed (BSD-style), and hosted on GitHub.  Its a fully native engine written around C++ reflection as a core technology.  Its contains the main implementation of C++ reflection I have been refining for a decade.
